solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Home not yet marvellous?

parts.note: the prefix pre- means before, i.e. not yet
fab is slang short for fabulous, marvellous

explanation.surface: A wry question about a house that has not yet become wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: PREFAB is a prefabricated house, a common post-war British stopgap home.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a factory-built house assembled on site, so it is a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Budget speech missing start?

indicators.note: missing its start tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Evokes the Chancellor's Budget speech with its opening lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Budget' looks like the Chancellor's annual statement, but it is the verb: to budget is to ration.
explanation.definitionFit: To budget a resource is to share it out carefully in limited amounts, the sense of the verb ration.

clue.text: Prevent everyone supporting Nottingham team?

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: Nottingham Forest is an English football club, known as Forest
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Fans everywhere backing Nottingham's football club, with a hint of stopping something.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act first so that something cannot happen, i.e. to head it off.

clue.text: Scarper when dice game finished

parts.note: beetle is a party dice game in which players draw a beetle part by part
off can mean finished or ended, as in a match being off

explanation.surface: Running away once the game of dice is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is a British party game where dice rolls decide which body part of a beetle you may draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetle off is British slang for hurrying away, the same as scarper.

clue.text: Heat-resistant layer quickly brought to vehicle

indicators.note: one piece is brought to another, placed after it in the answer

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace is an old-fashioned word for quickly

explanation.surface: A protective coating being rushed to a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is a hard protective shell, here a tough outer layer able to withstand heat or pressure.

clue.text: Agree Tories lure, sending out diamonds

parts.note: Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tories

indicators.note: sending out tells us these letters are expelled from the word for lure

parts.note: to entice is to lure
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Conservatives tempted to agree to something, with jewels cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE is underworld slang for diamonds; 'sending out' takes it from ENTICE, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to give permission or say yes, so it means agree.

clue.text: Bird losing wing and crest

indicators.note: losing tells us a stretch of the bird's name is shed

parts.note: a partridge is a game bird
a wing is a part or section, as of a building or party

explanation.surface: A bird missing a wing, with a crest on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops PART, a wing in the sense of a section, from PARTRIDGE. 'Crest' looks like the bird's plumage but is a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow hilltop, which is a crest of high ground.

clue.text: Round left in quiz

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to pump someone is to quiz them for information

explanation.surface: Reads like a quiz round with someone leaving partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' wants to be a quiz round; it is the adjective meaning rounded in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump describes a full, rounded figure, so it is a synonym for round.

clue.text: Slip beneath mountain pass and fall down

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece beneath comes after the other

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
a lapse is a slip or small error

explanation.surface: A climber slipping below a mountain pass and tumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to give way and drop suddenly, the same as to fall down.

clue.text: Doctor having to admit tense Scottish politician

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a surgeon is a doctor
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A doctor forced to confess something to a Scottish politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party and was Scotland's First Minister.

clue.text: Fix and mix blue drink

parts.note: to do a room is to fix it up

indicators.note: mix tells us the letters of blue are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Mixing up a blue cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a twice-sized measure of spirits, ordered as a drink in a bar.

clue.text: Fragment Oxford copper left

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the fictional Oxford detective of TV and novels

explanation.surface: An Oxford policeman leaving behind a scrap of evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is Colin Dexter's Oxford police detective, famous from British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece or scrap, especially of food, so it is a fragment.

clue.text: Former barrister has no time for model

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: has no tells us a letter is taken away from the barrister

parts.note: a Templar is a lawyer with chambers in the Temple, an Inn of Court in London

explanation.surface: An ex-lawyer too busy for a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inner and Middle Temple are London's barristers' Inns, whose members are Templars.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is an ideal example to copy, which is a model.

clue.text: Cleaner Frenchman put to work

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A Frenchman being given a job as a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mop is a tool for washing floors, so it is a cleaning implement.

clue.text: First-class mail? Guy's written in another guy's address

parts.note: A denotes first class, as in A1
post is mail

indicators.note: written in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to secure a tent or mast
a guy's belongings are his

explanation.surface: Posting a letter first class, with one man's name on another man's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' plays twice: as a man (his) and as a guy-rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To apostrophise is to speak directly to someone absent or abstract, a rhetorical way to address them.

clue.text: Runner, old, unexpectedly regains lead in race

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters land in a surprising new order
the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An aged athlete surprisingly retakes the lead in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like the athlete but is someone who runs an event; 'unexpectedly' rearranges REGAINS into RGANISE.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser is the person who runs an event or business, so a runner in that sense.

clue.text: Bush ranger skinned and eaten by Lernaean monster?

indicators.note: being eaten puts one piece inside the eater

parts.note: the Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Lerna slain by Heracles

indicators.note: skinned strips the outer letters off the word

explanation.surface: A flayed ranger devoured by a mythical many-headed beast in the bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' removes the ends of RANGER, leaving ANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrangea is a flowering garden shrub, which is a bush.

clue.text: Nazis rue having redeployed for Overlord

indicators.note: redeployed troops are rearranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nazis regretting troop movements for Operation Overlord, the D-Day invasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlord' calls up the 1944 Normandy invasion, but here it means a feudal lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A suzerain is a sovereign or state holding power over a dependent ruler, an overlord.

clue.text: Down finished and set to go up?

definitions.text: Down finished and set to go up?

parts.words: Down finished and set to go up?
parts.note: a young bird whose downy feathers are complete is ready to take off

explanation.surface: Something lowered, done, and about to rise again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' is feathers, not a direction; a bird with its plumage complete is ready to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully fledged bird has grown all its feathers and can fly, hence fully developed.

clue.text: Still one must escape Himalayan monster

indicators.note: escape means the letter gets out of the word, so it is removed

parts.note: the yeti is the abominable snowman of the Himalayas
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lone climber fleeing the abominable snowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet as an adverb means even now or nevertheless, the same as still.

clue.text: European died in grip of Asian land mammal

indicators.note: held in another's grip, one piece sits inside it

parts.note: China is a country in Asia
D is the abbreviation for died, used in dates

explanation.surface: A European tourist dying in an Asian country, with an animal involved.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Contrasting detail in brogue

definitions.meaning: in design an ... is a small feature that stands out from the rest
a brogue is a regional, especially Irish, way of speaking

explanation.surface: Decorative stitching on a brogue shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Accent covers both a striking design touch and a distinctive regional pronunciation.

clue.text: Returning quietly, do penance in church monument

indicators.note: in tells us the turned letters sit inside the church
returning means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to atone is to do penance

explanation.surface: Coming back to church to quietly make amends before a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical direction piano; 'Returning' turns P and the penance word into ENOTAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a memorial to the dead buried elsewhere, a war monument.

clue.text: Alumnus represented at centre with large corporation?

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: at centre takes the middle three letters of the word

explanation.surface: A former student acting as representative for a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old jokey word for a pot belly, not a company. 'at centre' takes ESE from the middle of 'represented'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is humorous dated slang for a large paunch, so someone with one is very fat.

clue.text: Gather tea's brought up in the morning

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up moves letters to the top

parts.note: Assam is a strong Indian black tea
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Morning tea is served for everyone to gather round.
explanation.walkthrough: The AM at the end of ASSAM is 'brought up' to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or pile up a large quantity, so to gather.

clue.text: Subtlety is thrown out from trial

indicators.note: thrown out from means these letters are ejected from the other word

parts.note: a trial is a nuisance, something annoying to endure

explanation.surface: A case is thrown out of a court trial on a fine point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' suggests a court case; it means a trying thing, a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning or difference, a subtlety.

clue.text: Mineral compound strong ale naturally contains

indicators.note: contains tells us the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: A claim that strong beer naturally includes some mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Galena is lead sulphide, the chief ore of lead, a mineral compound.

clue.text: Drop into grave, radioactive ultimately: that's fall out

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dire means grave or serious
to sag is to drop or droop

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Radioactive waste being dropped into a grave and the fallout that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall out' plays on radioactive fallout but means quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out with someone is to quarrel, which is to disagree.

clue.text: Beneath ocean, endless anti-rust treatment needed

indicators.note: endless tells us the last letter is cut off

parts.note: underseal is a protective coating sprayed on a car's underside against rust

explanation.surface: A ship's hull needing endless rustproofing below the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDERSEAL is a British term for the bitumen coating applied under cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Undersea means situated or happening below the surface of the sea.

clue.text: In which scene one would see Merchant of Venice?

definitions.text: In which scene one would see Merchant of Venice?

parts.words: In which scene one would see Merchant of Venice?
parts.note: the Venetian trading quarter where Shakespeare's merchants do business

explanation.surface: A theatre question about where a Shakespeare play is staged.
explanation.walkthrough: The play's title points to the stage, but a real merchant of Venice traded on its famous bridge and market district.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is Venice's old commercial centre, named in the play as where merchants meet.
